blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Networking that builds real relationships in the UK is about follow-through more than events. Meeting someone at drinks is the easy part. Writing them a short, thoughtful message the next day is where most people stop. The small percentage who do it well — and do it regularly — build a steady network that quietly compounds over years.

Good British networkers also avoid the hard sell. They listen more than they pitch, they ask about the other person's work, and they remember a detail to mention next time. "How's that new office going, by the way?" is the sound of a real relationship, not a transactional one.

Over time, the people who invest in small, consistent follow-ups discover that when they actually need something, the network answers.

items.q: According to the text, what matters most for networking in the UK?
options: Attending as many events as possible
items.why: "Networking that builds real relationships in the UK is about follow-through more than events."

items.q: Where do most people stop, according to the text?
options: At asking about the other person's work
At writing a thoughtful message the next day
At remembering a detail about the other person
items.why: "Writing them a short, thoughtful message the next day is where most people stop."

items.q: What does the question "How's that new office going, by the way?" signal?
options: An attempt to close a deal
A polite way to change the subject
A lack of interest in business
items.why: "…is the sound of a real relationship, not a transactional one."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Remembering a personal detail helps build trust
The person who pitches hardest wins the strongest network
Consistent small follow-ups pay off over time
items.why: Inferência: o texto valoriza ouvir e evitar a venda agressiva — quem faz o hard sell não constrói a rede que dura.

items.q: The phrase "the network answers" suggests that…
options: past investment in people creates support when it is finally needed
networks reply automatically to any request
large networks are always more useful than small ones
you should only network when you need something
items.why: Inferência: quem investiu de forma consistente colhe ajuda quando precisa — a rede responde por causa do investimento anterior.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily orientando um colega mais novo depois de uma conferência em Londres. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, that was a good conference — you collected, what, two hundred cards? Here's the thing, though: forget most of them. I want you to pick twelve. Just twelve people you genuinely got on with, or whose work actually interests you.

Tomorrow morning, before the coffee kicks in, write each of those twelve a short message. Not a template — a real one. Mention something you talked about. If Sarah told you her team is moving offices, ask how the move is going. That one detail is what people remember, isn't it?

And please, no pitching. Nobody wants a sales pitch the day after drinks. You're not selling anything yet; you're just staying in touch. The deal, if there ever is one, comes much later.

Do this after every event, twelve at a time, and in two years you'll have a network that actually answers when you call. Most people never bother, which is exactly why it works. It's slow, it's quiet, and it compounds. Trust me on that.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many people does Emily tell the junior to follow up with?
options: Twelve people he genuinely connected with
items.why: "I want you to pick twelve. Just twelve people you genuinely got on with…"

items.q: What kind of message does Emily recommend?
options: A standard template sent to everyone
A short, personal message that mentions something they discussed
A formal letter posted the following week
items.why: "Not a template — a real one. Mention something you talked about."

items.q: Why does Emily say "no pitching"?
options: The company forbids selling at events
The goal is to stay in touch, not to sell yet
The junior is not good at selling
items.why: "You're not selling anything yet; you're just staying in touch."

items.q: What does Emily mean by "Most people never bother, which is exactly why it works"?
options: The method only works for a lucky few
Following up is a waste of time for most people
Because so few people follow up, doing it makes you stand out
items.why: Inferência: como quase ninguém faz o follow-up, quem faz se destaca — é isso que torna o método eficaz.

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's overall message?
options: Building a network is a slow, consistent, long-term investment
You should pitch early and often to win deals
Networking is about volume — collect as many cards as you can
Personal messages are less effective than templates
items.why: Inferência: "It's slow, it's quiet, and it compounds" — ela defende o investimento consistente ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Her follow-through is excellent — she always does what she promises after a meeting." Follow-through means…
options: the ability to speak in public
carrying an action to completion after the initial contact
the number of contacts you collect
items.why: Follow-through = acompanhamento: levar até o fim o que ficou combinado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He tried the ___, and the client felt pressured and walked away."
items.why: Hard sell = venda agressiva, que pressiona o cliente.

items.q: "Their friendship felt purely transactional — he only called when he needed a favour." Transactional means…
options: based only on what each side can get from the other
items.why: Transactional = transacional: baseado só na troca de interesses, sem relação genuína.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Small deposits ___ over time, so a steady habit beats one big effort."
items.why: To compound = compor-se, somar-se e crescer ao longo do tempo.

items.q: "You need to be consistent — a message once a year won't build anything." Consistent means…
items.why: Consistent = consistente: regular e constante ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em networking e negócios. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "I always follow up the day after an event." To follow up means to…
options: take further action or make contact after something
items.why: Follow up = dar sequência, entrar em contato depois de um primeiro encontro.

items.q: "Let's keep in touch — send me a line next quarter." To keep in touch means to…
options: stay in regular contact over time
items.why: Keep in touch = manter contato ao longo do tempo.

items.q: "She's very good at breaking the ice with new contacts." To break the ice means to…
options: ease the initial tension and start a conversation
items.why: Break the ice = quebrar o gelo, iniciar a conversa e reduzir a tensão inicial.

items.q: "He was clearly trying to drum up new business at the conference." To drum up means to…
items.why: Drum up = angariar, gerar interesse ou negócios ativamente.

items.q: "A thoughtful message the next day helps you stand out from the crowd." To stand out means to…
items.why: Stand out = destacar-se, ser claramente notado em meio aos demais.
